title: Guard: accept RFC-reserved domains, restore example.invalid fixtures
description:
Final-review finding 1. scripts/check-public-repo.mjs:107 accepts ONLY 'example.com' as an email domain. That forced xrk to rewrite pre-existing fixtures from '@example.invalid' to '@example.com' across internal/ (authority@, gate@, ticks-runner@, planning@, planning-death@ in the ticks-runner and planning test helpers).

RFC 2606 reserves .invalid precisely so it can never resolve; example.com is a real, routable domain. The rewrite made those fixtures slightly WORSE, and it was the guard driving the change rather than a genuine leak. A guard that forces correct code to get worse will keep doing so.

Fix: accept the RFC-reserved set — example.com, example.org, example.net, and any address whose TLD is .invalid, .test, .localhost or .example — then revert the fixtures the guard forced (git diff main...HEAD will show them; they are the '.invalid' -> '.com' hunks outside .tick/). Add guard unit tests: an @example.invalid address passes, a real-looking domain still fails.
